cards.text: Hezekiah, king of Judah, becomes deadly sick. Then Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, comes to him with a word from the LORD. Friend, when the prophet makes a house call, you sit UP.

cards.question: Isaiah brings the deadly sick Hezekiah a word from the LORD. What does it tell the king to do?
The LORD's message through Isaiah says Hezekiah will recover from this illness.

cards.text: Hezekiah turns his face to the wall, and he prays to the LORD.

cards.question: Facing the wall, Hezekiah prays. What does he ask the LORD to remember?

answers.text: How he has walked faithfully before Him
How much gold he has given the temple
How many battles he has won for Judah

cards.question: With his face to the wall, Hezekiah prays to the LORD and ___ bitterly.

cards.text: Now watch this. The word of the LORD comes to Isaiah, and it's a message for Hezekiah.

cards.question: The LORD, the God of Hezekiah's father David, sends Isaiah back to the king. What does the LORD say He has done?

answers.text: Heard his prayer and seen his tears
Sent an angel to heal his body
Chosen a son to reign after him

cards.question: The LORD says He will add ___ years to Hezekiah's life.

cards.text: I hit snooze and get nine minutes, but Hezekiah prays and gets FIFTEEN YEARS! And the LORD's not done, because there's a promise for the city too.

cards.question: The LORD promises to deliver Hezekiah and the city from the hand of which king?
Along with that promise, the LORD also says He will defend the city.

cards.text: Then comes a sign from the LORD, so Hezekiah will know the LORD will do what He has promised.

cards.question: The LORD's sign for Hezekiah involves the sun's shadow on the stairway of Ahaz. What will the LORD make the shadow do?

answers.text: Stop on one step all day

cards.question: The shadow on the stairway of Ahaz never actually moves back.

cards.text: After his illness and recovery, Hezekiah, king of Judah, writes about it. He starts with what he said back when it looked like the end: in the prime of his life, he'd go through the gates of Sheol.

cards.question: Back when Hezekiah thought he was dying, who did he say he'd never again see in the land of the living?

cards.text: Then Hezekiah paints pictures. His dwelling was picked up and removed from him like a shepherd's tent.

cards.question: Hezekiah has another picture. He says he has rolled up his life like a weaver, and He cuts him off from the ___.

cards.text: Then Hezekiah says, "Like a lion He breaks all my bones; from day until night You make an end of me."
He chirps like a swallow or crane and moans like a dove. Friend, I make that dove sound every time a whole tray slides off the rack.

cards.question: Weak and oppressed, Hezekiah looks upward and asks the Lord to be his ___.

cards.text: Then Hezekiah says, "What can I say? He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done this."

cards.question: Hezekiah says that because of the anguish of his soul, he will walk slowly all his years.

cards.text: Then he says it to the Lord plain as dough: "You have restored me to health and have let me live."

cards.question: Looking back, Hezekiah says all his great anguish was for nothing.
Hezekiah says the Lord's love delivered him from the pit of oblivion. And his sins? Where has the Lord cast them?

cards.text: Behind His BACK, friend, and I can't get a burnt batch that far out of sight! Then Hezekiah says Sheol cannot thank the Lord, and Death cannot praise Him.

cards.question: If Sheol and Death can't thank the Lord, who does Hezekiah say can?
Hezekiah says fathers will tell their children about the Lord's ___.

cards.text: He ends with this: "The LORD will save me; we will play songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD." Fifteen more years, and the king is putting a band together.
Now the writing is done, and the passage looks back at two things from earlier. First, Isaiah had given an order about Hezekiah's boil.

cards.question: What had Isaiah said to prepare and apply to Hezekiah's boil so he would recover?
Hezekiah had also asked what the sign would be that he would go up to the house of the LORD.

cards.text: And that's where we leave King Hezekiah for now. Keep that apron on, friend, because his story's not finished.

findings.problem: Stop 1 follows a fixed pattern. Every story card (1, 4, 7, 10, 13) is followed right away by a multiple choice card, and then usually a second card of another type. Multiple choice also makes up 5 of the 10 choice cards, against only 2 fill in the blank cards.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The wrong answers are not believable. Hezekiah could never 'again' see his father David or the prophet Elijah in the land of the living, because both were long gone before his time and he had never seen them. That makes 'The LORD' the only answer that fits the question, so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The line saying the story isn't over copies the doc's example almost word for word: 'And that's where we leave King Hezekiah for now' against the example 'And that's where we'll leave it for now.'

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank sentence mixes tenses: 'Hezekiah prays to the LORD and ___ bitterly.' The right answer is 'wept,' which is past tense, while 'prays' is present tense. All three answers are past tense, so whichever one the baker picks, the sentence reads ungrammatically.
findings.question: Should fill in the blank sentences have to read grammatically with the right answer filled in? If so, should that rule be added to prep-walkthrough.md, and should this card be reworded, for example to 'weeps' with matching present-tense wrong answers?
